---
title: "Counterbalancing"
execute:
  cache: false
---

ManyBabies 1 used four pseudorandom trial orders to distribute register and paired stimulus identity over the sixteen test positions. Each order contained four alternating blocks, each with two infant-directed-speech (IDS) and two adult-directed-speech (ADS) trials. The same IDS and ADS stimulus numbers formed pairs. We can recover the realized order templates from the [released trial table](units-of-assignment.qmd).

```{r}
manybabies <- readRDS("data/manybabies/manybabies1-trials.rds")

stopifnot(
  nrow(manybabies) == 37264L,
  setequal(stats::na.omit(unique(manybabies$register)), c("ADS", "IDS")),
  setequal(stats::na.omit(unique(manybabies$counterbalance_order)), 1:4),
  setequal(stats::na.omit(unique(manybabies$stimulus_id)), 1:8)
)

recorded_design <- manybabies[
  manybabies$trial_metadata_observed &
    !is.na(manybabies$counterbalance_order),
]

mode_value <- function(x) {
  counts <- sort(table(x, useNA = "no"), decreasing = TRUE)
  names(counts)[[1L]]
}
```

[**Counterbalancing**](https://opentextbc.ca/researchmethods/chapter/experimental-design/) constrains how conditions and materials are distributed across orders. It does not create independent trials. In this study, the constraint makes register available within infant while distributing register and paired stimulus identity over trial position.

## Reconstructing the order templates

Protocol deviations mean that the released rows need not agree perfectly within every order-by-position cell. We recover the modal register and stimulus number for each cell, then check the resulting template.

```{r}
template_register <- aggregate(
  register ~ counterbalance_order + trial_number,
  data = recorded_design,
  FUN = mode_value
)

template_stimulus <- aggregate(
  stimulus_id ~ counterbalance_order + trial_number,
  data = recorded_design,
  FUN = function(x) as.integer(mode_value(x))
)

order_template <- merge(
  template_register,
  template_stimulus,
  by = c("counterbalance_order", "trial_number")
)
order_template <- order_template[
  order(order_template$counterbalance_order, order_template$trial_number),
]
names(order_template)[1L] <- "assigned_order"

balance_checks <- lapply(1:4, function(order) {
  current <- order_template[order_template$assigned_order == order, ]
  register_counts <- table(current$register)
  pair_counts <- table(current$stimulus_id)
  pair_by_register <- table(current$stimulus_id, current$register)

  stopifnot(
    nrow(current) == 16L,
    all(register_counts == 8L),
    all(pair_counts == 2L),
    all(pair_by_register == 1L)
  )

  data.frame(
    assigned_order = order,
    positions = nrow(current),
    ads_positions = unname(register_counts[["ADS"]]),
    ids_positions = unname(register_counts[["IDS"]]),
    paired_stimuli = length(pair_counts),
    one_of_each_register_per_pair = all(pair_by_register == 1L)
  )
})

balance_checks <- do.call(rbind, balance_checks)
knitr::kable(balance_checks)
```

Let $R_{ot}$ and $P_{ot}$ denote the modal register and paired stimulus at position $t$ in order $o$. The checks above establish the empirical margins

$$
\sum_t I(R_{ot}=\mathrm{IDS})
=\sum_t I(R_{ot}=\mathrm{ADS})=8,
$$

and, for every pair $p$ in every order $o$,

$$
\sum_t I(P_{ot}=p)=2,
\qquad
\sum_t I(P_{ot}=p,R_{ot}=r)=1
$$

for each register $r$. Thus every paired stimulus occurs once as IDS and once as ADS within an order.

## A restrained order map

The tile plot shows the register margin without placing a label in every cell. Pair identity remains checked in the code and table rather than added as sixty-four annotations.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.4
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-alt: "Four trial-order rows across sixteen positions, with gray adult-directed and blue infant-directed speech tiles."

ggplot2::ggplot(
  order_template,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = trial_number,
    y = factor(assigned_order),
    fill = register
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.45) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(ADS = "grey78", IDS = "#2C6E9B") # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(
      min(order_template$trial_number),
      4L * seq_len(max(order_template$trial_number) / 4L)
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Trial number", y = "Assigned order", fill = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Each order contains both registers across the session rather than placing all IDS trials before all ADS trials. The four orders use different position patterns, which distributes a register contrast over earlier and later positions across infants.

## Planned template and released records

The modal template is a reconstruction from the release. We can compare every recorded metadata row with the relevant modal cell.

```{r}
template_key <- paste(order_template$assigned_order, order_template$trial_number)
register_lookup <- setNames(order_template$register, template_key)
stimulus_lookup <- setNames(order_template$stimulus_id, template_key)

recorded_key <- paste(
  recorded_design$counterbalance_order,
  recorded_design$trial_number
)

recorded_design$register_matches_template <-
  recorded_design$register == unname(register_lookup[recorded_key])
recorded_design$stimulus_matches_template <-
  recorded_design$stimulus_id == unname(stimulus_lookup[recorded_key])

template_match <- data.frame(
  recorded_metadata_rows = nrow(recorded_design),
  register_match_proportion = mean(recorded_design$register_matches_template),
  stimulus_match_proportion = mean(recorded_design$stimulus_matches_template)
)

knitr::kable(
  template_match,
  digits = 4,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The modal register template agrees with `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * template_match$register_match_proportion)` of recorded metadata rows, and the modal stimulus template agrees with `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * template_match$stimulus_match_proportion)`. These are agreement rates with the modal released pattern after documented protocol deviations. They are not coder-accuracy estimates.

## What counterbalancing does not do

Counterbalancing separates register from a fixed position and paired stimulus in the planned sequence. It does not remove dependence: trials still repeat within infants, stimuli recur across infants, and infants remain nested within laboratories. Nor does balance verify how infants were allocated to sequences. That claim remains subject to the [allocation-verification boundary](random-assignment.qmd).

::: {.callout-note title="Audit the realized counterbalance"}
1. Which margin verifies equal IDS and ADS counts within an order?
2. Which margin verifies one IDS and one ADS occurrence for each paired stimulus?
3. Why is a modal template needed for this release?
4. Why does balanced sequencing not make trial rows independent?
:::

Counterbalancing distributes register and paired stimulus identity over order and position. The released template satisfies the intended margins, while a small share of metadata rows departs from the modal pattern. The next page distinguishes these recorded rows from rows removed or completed by the [exclusion pipeline](exclusion-rules.qmd).
